The initial steps are from this YouTube [tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OlvO-EG-P60).

Briefly, I created a new Quarto Blog project in Rstudio, which creates a set of 
template files to start with. The `index.qmd` file is formatted as a blog, so I 
renamed it to `blog.qmd`. Then I renamed the `about.qmd` file to `index.qmd` to 
use as the site home page. Then I updated the `_quarto.yml` file to 
add a nav bar to the left hand side as shown in the video. And I removed the 
example blog posts as well. I also added a line to change the directory where 
the website is created when it is rendered.
This is done by adding this line to the project section of `_quarto.yml`
```
  output-dir: "docs"
```

Now, when I render the website, it is created in a `docs` folder.
The default theme is [Cosmo](https://bootswatch.com/cosmo/), which I kept, but I
also added a optional dark theme, [Superhero](https://bootswatch.com/superhero/)

Once the initial set up was done, I set about customising the `Home` page by 
editing the `index.qmd` file.

First, I added a profile picture. Initially, the `index.qmd` file has a default
profile picture `profile.jpg`. I created an `assets` folder and an `images` 
folder within that. In there, I put a picture of me named `profile.jpg` and I 
changed the filename in the YAML to `assets/images/profile.jpg`.

Then in the `index.qmd` file, I added some text about me and some images.
The images were also placed in the `assets/images` folder. An image is normally
rendered as a block element on its own line, but I wanted to have all three on 
the same line. So, I put them inside a div element using
```
::: {#example-plots style="background-color: #FFFFFF"}
![](assets/images/zfs-fig1b.png){width=30%}
![](assets/images/top1000-var-high-res.png){width=30%}
![](assets/images/shigella-heatmap.png){width=30%}
:::
```
I made sure the images all fitted by adding `{width=30%}`.  
The `style="background-color: #FFFFFF"` makes sure there is a consistent 
background in dark mode.

Finally,I wanted to remove the link to the bin fire that is Twitter and change 
it to Bluesky and add a link to my [ORCiD](https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1842-412X) 
page. This has a list of my publications. The Bluesky and ORCiD icons are not 
in the standard bootstrap icons, but are provided in the set of free [FontAwesome](https://fontawesome.com/search?q=orcid&o=r&ic=free) icons. 
So I installed the Quarto [Font Awesome extension](https://github.com/quarto-ext/fontawesome)

```
quarto add quarto-ext/fontawesome
```

The Bluesky and ORCiD logos are in the brands set, so the shortcodes for them are:

```markdown
{{{< fa brands bluesky >}}}
{{{< fa brands orcid >}}}
```

A slight wrinkle is that instead of using the icon key as in the github and 
twitter examples, you need to use the text key, as explained [here](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/7640).

So the yaml in the frontmatter of the `index.qmd` file looks like this:
```markdown
title: "Richard White"
image: assets/images/profile.jpg
about:
  template: jolla
  links:
    - icon: github
      text: Github
      href: https://github.com/richysix
    - text: "{{{< fa brands bluesky >}}} Bluesky"
      href: https://bsky.app/profile/richysix.bsky.social
    - text: "{{{< fa brands orcid >}}} ORCiD"
      href: https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1842-412X
```

And the buttons look like this: 

![](orcid-logo.png)
![](bluesky-logo.png)

There are similar links in the `_quarto.yml` file for the nav bar.
